supportingReads: committed GLBs: ctx-hemisphere-l, ctx-putamen-l, ctx-globus-pallidus-l, ctx-caudate-l, ctx-hippocampus-l, ctx-amygdala-l, ctx-corpus-callosum, ctx-fornix-l, tel-lateral-ventricle-l
src/components/section/corticalLobes.ts (CORTICAL_BOUNDARIES / classifyCorticalPoint — read only, not changed)
scope.method: Per-record, per-field review of all 71 telencephalon structure records. Position was measured, not eyeballed: every origin3d was tested against the committed ctx-hemisphere-l GLB (40,388 vertices) by nearest-vertex projection with a signed test against the vertex normal, and the deep structures against their own committed meshes (inside/outside parity ray casts plus coronal bounding boxes). Somatotopy ordering was checked as a monotone sequence along the strip. No data file was edited.
scope.notAudited: Glyral plate labels (owned by the tracts/plates auditor); vasculature territory lists except where cited as a basis; the 23 records of tracts.json except tract-optic-radiation, which the brief assigns here.

findings.claimed: [43.2, 66.5, 19] — contextNote: 'the origin3d anchor was probed from that ribbon by the v8 content-authoring run'
findings.expected: an anchor inside the precentral strip defined by ctx-m1's own eight somatotopy children; on the measured strip that means z between about −13 and −4 at this y (e.g. the ctx-m1-tongue anchor [46.49, 68.5, −4.39] lies 23.7 au away)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — ctx-m1 is the TAXONOMY PARENT of ctx-m1-toe…ctx-m1-larynx (taxonomy.json carries "parent":"ctx-m1" on all eight), and those eight are the measured precentral strip: each sits on a ctx-hemisphere-l vertex with residual 0.00–0.01 au (own measurement, probe-signed). ctx-m1's own z = 19 is 22.4 au (26.9 mm) anterior to the strip's anterior limit z = −3.51 and 23.7 au from its nearest child; the marker and every child patch are disjoint volumes (ctx-m1 ± size3d z = 12…26 against the strip's z = −12.8…−3.5). It is also 38.2 au (45.9 mm) from the strip centroid.
findings.suggestedFix: Move ctx-m1 origin3d onto its own strip, e.g. [45.0, 70.0, −4.5] (the ctx-m1-tongue/larynx anchor region, on the ribbon at residual < 0.1 au, inside CLIP_BOUNDS, laterality paired +x preserved). Alternative if the whole M1 strip is thought wrong: do NOT move ctx-m1 alone — the eight children are the measured ones and outrank it.
findings.notes: The record is a context envelope, so this is a marker/locator defect, not a geometry defect. Second-order check that fails too: the record's own anchor text says 'precentral gyrus — the anterior wall of the central sulcus, medial surface foot representation included', and 19 au anterior of the strip at x = 43.2 is middle-frontal-gyrus territory on this ribbon. The shipped cortical-division rule calls this point 'parietal' (classifyCorticalPoint(43.2, 66.5, 19) → parietal, boundary z ≥ 5 at y < 77), which is a consequence of the rule's fitted central-sulcus constant, not independent proof.

findings.claimed: [42.4, 68.2, −1.7] — contextNote: 'probed from that ribbon'
findings.expected: an anchor inside the postcentral strip defined by ctx-s1's own eight children; on the measured strip that means z between about −21 and −9 at this y (the nearest children are ctx-s1-tongue [46.37, 68.13, −14.62] and ctx-s1-larynx [50.86, 60.88, −9.24], both 13.5 au away)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — ctx-s1 is the taxonomy parent of the eight ctx-s1-* somatotopy records ("parent":"ctx-s1" on all eight), each measured on a ctx-hemisphere-l vertex (residual 0.00–0.01 au, own measurement). ctx-s1's z = −1.7 is 7.5 au (9.0 mm) anterior to the strip's anterior limit z = −9.24 and 13.5 au (16.2 mm) from its nearest child; centroid offset 27.2 au = 32.7 mm. The S1 strip is additionally the posterior of the two strips (all eight sit behind their M1 counterparts at the same body part, 4.4–10.5 au), so the S1 anchor being anterior to the M1 strip's children (−3.5…−12.8) inverts the one ordering the atlas itself asserts.
findings.suggestedFix: Move ctx-s1 origin3d onto its own strip, e.g. [46.5, 66.0, −13.5] (between the ctx-s1-tongue and ctx-s1-larynx anchors, on the ribbon at residual < 0.1 au, inside CLIP_BOUNDS).
findings.notes: Same defect class and same cause as T3-0001: the two context anchors describe a precentral/postcentral strip pair but were placed 20+ au anterior of the strip pair the atlas measures. Fixing one without the other leaves the pair inconsistent.

findings.claimed: [6, 82.8, 22.6] — anchor text: 'medial superior frontal gyrus … above the cingulate sulcus (mesial area 6, posterior part)'
findings.expected: an anchor immediately anterior to the medial foot representation it must abut, i.e. within about 10–15 au of ctx-m1-toe [7.46, 109.89, −11.91]; measured offset from that segment is [−1.5, −27.1, +34.5] au
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — the record's own function text says the SMA is 'on the dorsomedial surface of the hemisphere, in front of the medial M1 foot representation', and the apex of the medial surface is measured at y = 113.6 (ctx-hemisphere-l vertex maximum, own measurement). ctx-sma sits at y = 82.8, i.e. 30.9 au (37 mm) BELOW the medial apex and 27.1 au below ctx-m1-toe, while the y-gap to ctx-m1-toe in the same ribbon is 34.5 au (41.4 mm). No placement can be both 'in front of the foot representation' and 41 mm away from it on a hemisphere whose medial surface spans y 113.6 down to the callosum.
findings.suggestedFix: Move ctx-sma origin3d anterior to ctx-m1-toe on the medial surface, the same z-band but ~12–18 au anterior: e.g. [5.5, 106.0, 4.0] (check on the ribbon: the medial surface at x ≈ 5–6 spans y 0…113, z −70…+66, so this lands on it; residual must be re-probed before use).
findings.notes: This record has no somatotopy children, so the internal contradiction is against ctx-m1-toe (its direct neighbour in the homunculus) rather than a child. The record's level set (lvl-tel-centrum-semiovale, lvl-tel-convexity) already implies the convexity/vertex region, which its origin3d does not occupy.

findings.recordId: ctx-s1-toe, ctx-s1-leg, ctx-s1-trunk, ctx-s1-arm, ctx-s1-hand, ctx-s1-face, ctx-s1-tongue, ctx-s1-larynx
findings.claimed: ctx-s1-toe 'the paracentral lobule and the medial end of the precentral gyrus'; ctx-s1-leg 'the leg band of the precentral gyrus'; ctx-s1-trunk 'superior convexity of the precentral gyrus'; ctx-s1-arm 'upper lateral convexity of the precentral gyrus (arm band)'; ctx-s1-hand 'lateral convexity of the precentral gyrus at the hand-knob'; ctx-s1-face 'lower lateral convexity of the precentral gyrus (face band), above the lateral fissure'; ctx-s1-tongue and ctx-s1-larynx 'opercular surface of the precentral gyrus …'
findings.expected: 'postcentral gyrus' (or 'postcentral bank of the central sulcus') in place of 'precentral gyrus' in all eight anchors, since the records are the S1 strip
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — each record's own strip field is "strip":"S1 (postcentral)", its name is 'Primary somatosensory cortex (S1) — … representation', its function text says 'the most lateral of the large representations, on the opercular surface' in the sensory strip, and the shipped gate scripts/verify/somatotopy.mjs asserts the M1/S1 pairing by body part. The gyrus in the anchors is copy-paste from the ctx-m1-* records, which carry the identical nine texts.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'precentral gyrus' with 'postcentral gyrus' in the eight ctx-s1-* anchors.gyrus strings (text-only change; anchors.surfaceNormal, anchors.somatotopicOrder, origin3d and every measured number stay as they are).
findings.notes: Suspicion that it is MORE than a naming slip was tested and is not supported: the S1 patch sits 4.23–10.23 au posterior to its M1 counterpart in z for all eight body parts (total offset 4.45–10.53 au = 5.3–12.6 mm), which is the correct postcentral relation, so only the label is wrong, not the geometry. This is the one systematic nomenclature defect in the somatotopy table.

findings.claimed: 'The record is positioned on the medial concave edge of the baked hippocampal cast (x ≈ 21.5, y ≈ 12, z ≈ −9, probed from ctx-hippocampus-l …)'
findings.expected: the coordinates the record actually carries: origin3d [16, 14, −2] — nearest ctx-hippocampus-l vertex [21.05, 13.33, −2.76], 5.15 au away (own measurement)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — the contextNote and origin3d are fields of the same record, and they disagree by 6.6 au in x and 7 au in z. Every sibling subfield record's note matches its own origin3d exactly (nuc-subiculum 20.7/11.8/0.6, nuc-ca1 24.8/13.8/−0.9, nuc-ca2-ca3 28.1/13/−4.1, nuc-ca4 25.1/12.7/−1.2 — all quoted verbatim in their notes and all confirmed against the file).
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite the parenthetical to the committed value: '(x ≈ 16, y ≈ 14, z ≈ −2, probed from ctx-hippocampus-l …)'. Do not move origin3d: [16, 14, −2] is 5.9 au ventral-medial of the hippocampal cast and is the defensible anatomy (the dentate blade is the medial-most of the hippocampal fields, and the note's own x ≈ 21.5 would sit on top of nuc-ca1 at 24.8).
findings.notes: Also checked and passing: nuc-dentate-gyrus laterality is 'paired' with x = +16 (one-side convention), and nuc-dentate (the cerebellar nucleus, y = −24.7…−19.3) is a different record in medulla.json — the two ids do not collide.

findings.claimed: 'Entorhinal cortex layer II and hilar mossy cells; CA2 additionally receives dense supramammillary and hypothalamic input'
findings.expected: 'Hilar mossy cells and CA3 recurrent collaterals; the entorhinal projection to CA3 is from layer II (perforant path to the distal dendrites) but the dense layer-III temporoammonic input goes to CA1/subiculum, and CA2's defining input is hypothalamic (supramammillary/vasopressin). Layer II should not be listed as a shared CA2/CA3 afferent in the same item as the mossy cells.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the sibling records of the same file — nuc-ca1 states the circuit correctly ('CA3 through the Schaffer collateral-commissural system … Entorhinal cortex layer III through the temporoammonic path … the direct, trisynaptic-bypassing input'), and nuc-dentate-gyrus states 'Perforant path from the entorhinal cortex (layer II) onto granule-cell dendrites'. The CA2/CA3 item collapses layer II (a dentate/CA3 input) with 'hilar mossy cells' (a dentate/hilus population) as one CA2+CA3 afferent, which reads as if CA2 takes the layer-II perforant path directly. My own anatomical knowledge, labelled as such.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the item: 'Dentate gyrus granule cells through the mossy fibres (CA3 proximal dendrites); hilar mossy cells and CA3 recurrent collaterals; entorhinal layer II perforant-path fibres to the distal CA3 dendrites; CA2 additionally receives dense supramammillary and hypothalamic (vasopressin) input.'
findings.notes: No direction error (the afferent/efferent split of the trisynaptic circuit is right in this record: dentate→CA3 under afferent, CA3→CA1/subiculum under efferent).

findings.claimed: name 'Secondary auditory cortex (A2, planum temporale)'; synonyms ['A2', 'Brodmann area 42', 'auditory association cortex', 'planum temporale', 'belt and parabelt auditory cortex']; anchors.gyrus 'planum temporale — the posterior superior temporal plane behind Heschl's gyrus (registered separately as surf-planum-temporale)'
findings.expected: the record separates two things the atlas elsewhere keeps apart: Brodmann 42 is on Heschl's gyrus (the A1 belt), while the planum temporale is the region behind it
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the atlas' own A1 record and with the separately registered surface record — ctx-a1 claims 'transverse temporal gyri of Heschl' and 'Brodmann area 41' for the Heschl gyrus, so 'Brodmann area 42 = planum temporale' makes area 42 (which overlies Heschl's gyrus) land where area 41 already is; and surf-planum-temporale exists as its own taxonomy row with the synonym 'auditory association cortex of the superior temporal plane', duplicating this record's anchor. The two anchors are 2.1 au apart (ctx-a2 [35, 33.5, 2] vs surf-planum-temporale [33, 34, 2], own measurement), so the two records mark the same patch.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the id and the host but fix the equation: name 'Secondary auditory cortex (A2) / planum temporale region', synonyms drop the bare 'Brodmann area 42' or qualify it as 'Brodmann area 42 (Heschl's gyrus belt) and area 22 (planum temporale)', and change anchors.gyrus to 'posterior superior temporal plane behind Heschl's gyrus (registered separately as surf-planum-temporale) — the record is the area-level view of that surface'. No coordinate change needed.
findings.notes: This is the one place in the cortical-area set where two records make the same claim about the same patch of ribbon; the FEF/premotor pair and the M1/S1 pair do not overlap (3.6 au and 4.3 au apart respectively, both with distinct Brodmann assignments 8 vs 6 and 4 vs 3a/3b/1/2).

findings.claimed: 'Brodmann areas 44 and 45' presented as the definition of Broca's area, with synonyms 'inferior frontal gyrus, opercular and triangular parts'
findings.expected: 'Brodmann area 44 (pars opercularis), with area 45 (pars triangularis) as its anterior extension' — area 45 is not coextensive with Broca's area, and the modern boundary discussion makes that explicit
findings.basis: My own anatomical knowledge, labelled as such (the classic 44+45 equation overstates the pars triangularis; the opercular/opercular-triangular boundary and the 44/45 border are both contested in the modern literature the brief asks about). Corroborrated internally: the record's own function text already says 'pars opercularis and triangularis, Brodmann 44/45', i.e. it treats the two areas as the two parts, which is the equation the synonym list asserts flatly.
findings.suggestedFix: Rephrase the synonym to 'Brodmann area 44 (pars opercularis) and 45 (pars triangularis) — the 44/45 border is debated' and keep the id.
findings.notes: Everything else in this record checked out and was left alone: the pars opercularis/triangularis location, the arcuate (superior longitudinal) input from Wernicke's area, the corticobulbar output to the CN V/VII/IX/X/XII nuclei, and the MCA superior-division vascular attribution for Broca aphasia.

findings.claimed: 'The anterior, bulging third of the C-shaped striatum, filling the wall of the frontal horn'
findings.expected: 'forming the lateral wall of the frontal horn'
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the same file plus the committed geometry — nuc-caudate-body says the body 'l[ies] in the floor of the lateral ventricle body', and the committed tel-lateral-ventricle-l mesh measures x 0.7…11.9 at z = 30 (own measurement), i.e. the frontal horn is MEDIAL to the caudate head (ctx-caudate-l x 5.0…15.9 at the same z): the head abuts the horn's lateral wall and does not fill it. nuc-caudate-tail's statement ('arcs downward behind the thalamus into the roof of the temporal horn') is correct and shows the file knows the difference.
findings.suggestedFix: 'filling the lateral wall of the frontal horn'
findings.notes: Text-only. The rest of the record (associative/limbic striatum, Heubner supply, head-of-caudate infarct with abulia, Huntington disease) is correct as written.

findings.claimed: 'Lenticulostriate branches of the MCA and the anterior choroidal artery (which supplies the inferior/posterior pallidum together with the posterior limb of the internal capsule and the optic radiation)'
findings.expected: 'contralateral hemiplegia, hemianaesthesia and hemianopia' attributed to the posterior limb of the internal capsule + the optic radiation/thalamus; the anterior choroidal artery is not the usual supply of the pallidum
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — the same file's nuc-putamen records 'the inferior and posterior parts also receive anterior choroidal branches' for the PUTAMEN, and nuc-globus-pallidus-externus independently claims 'anterior choroidal artery for the inferior and posterior part'. Textbook teaching (Blumenfeld/Patten, the records' own reference list) puts pallidal supply with the lenticulostriate perforators and the anterior choroidal territory with the posterior limb, the optic radiation and the medial temporal lobe, not the pallidum. My own anatomical knowledge, labelled as such, agreeing with the sibling-record pattern.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the anterior-choroidal attribution from the pallidal BLOOD text and from nuc-globus-pallidus-externus, keeping it only where the same record describes the capsular/optic-radiation triad (as nuc-caudate-tail and nuc-putamen already do).
findings.notes: Only the attribution is at issue; the ansa lenticularis / lenticular fasciculus H2 → thalamic fasciculus H1 output and the centromedian collateral in this record are correct.

findings.claimed: ['lvl-thalamus-rostral', 'lvl-tel-thalamostriate']
findings.expected: ['lvl-thalamus-rostral'] (or a level set that reaches a level the record's own course occupies)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — levels and waypoints are fields of the same record. The five waypoints span y 19…23.5 (z 23.5…33), so the highest plane the course reaches is y ≈ 23.5; lvl-tel-thalamostriate is anchored at y = 48 (src/data/levels.json), i.e. 24.5 au = 29.4 mm above the top of the record's own course. This is the same defect class as the pre-existing tract-optic-radiation finding recorded by the architect review (waypoints y 14…30 against levels reaching y = 78), which is the identical pattern inside the same anatomical system.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop 'lvl-tel-thalamostriate' from tract-optic-nerve.levels, leaving ['lvl-thalamus-rostral']. The rendered level chips jump the slice plane, so the chip currently lands the user 24 au above the optic nerve.
findings.notes: The record has no levels whose anchors lie below its course, so no level is missing; the fix is a removal, not an addition.

findings.claimed: levels ['lvl-midbrain-sc','lvl-post-comm','lvl-thalamus-mid','lvl-thalamus-rostral','lvl-tel-thalamostriate','lvl-tel-convexity'] against waypoints [[18,16,−6],[23,20,6],[27,15,12],[28,14,−14],[24,20,−34],[20,27,−52],[13,30,−66]]
findings.expected: either the levels drop lvl-tel-thalamostriate (y = 48) and lvl-tel-convexity (y = 78), or the course is extended to reach V1 around the calcarine fissure, which the record's own function text says is its target: 'Primary visual cortex (V1, striate cortex) around the calcarine fissure', whose record ctx-v1 carries size3d [4,4,5] at [9.5,17,−60]
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — the waypoints span y 14…30, so both of the highest two level anchors (y = 48 and y = 78) lie 18 au and 48 au beyond the record's own course, while the record's stated target is the occipital calcarine cortex (level lvl-tel-convexity region, y = 78). Independently reported by the architect review as pre-existing defect D2; this audit re-measured it from the file and confirms both the numbers and the level/waypoint mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Preferred: extend waypoints past [13,30,−66] to the V1 anchor region (ctx-v1 [9.5,17,−60], whose own level set reaches lvl-tel-convexity) with a waypoint near [11,26,−66] — the LGN→V1 radiation does reach the calcarine cortex and the record's own target sentence demands it. If the course is deliberately truncated to the sagittal-stratum segment, then remove lvl-tel-thalamostriate and lvl-tel-convexity from levels and say so in contextNote.
findings.notes: tracts.json is owned by the tracts/plates auditor for every other row; this row is inside the telencephalon assignment (optic pathway) and is reported here so the integrator sees both reviews of the same row. No change was made.

findings.claimed: [16.4, 33, −50] — anchors.mesh 'ctx-hemisphere-l' (the record is a 'view over its host gyrus')
findings.expected: an anchor on the ribbon surface; the nearest ctx-hemisphere-l vertex to this point measures 5.56 au (6.7 mm) away and every nearest vertex normal points outward past it (signed distance −5.56 au, i.e. 5.56 au INSIDE the ribbon)
findings.basis: Measured against the committed mesh (basis = committed GLB, ctx-hemisphere-l, 40,388 vertices; nearest-vertex projection + vertex-normal sign, own measurement). Every other ctx-hemisphere-l-anchored cortical area sits within 1.2 au of the surface (ctx-v1 2.69, ctx-a1 0.31, ctx-a2 0.57, ctx-wernicke 1.14, ctx-broca 0.64, ctx-m1 0.27, ctx-s1 0.56, ctx-premotor 0.83, ctx-sma 0.73, ctx-entorhinal 0.99, ctx-frontal-eye-fields 0.86), with ctx-v2 the single outlier at 5.56 au; the v8 contextNote states that every one of these anchors 'was probed from that ribbon'.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-probe ctx-v2 onto the ribbon with the nearest-vertex method the other ten areas used. The nearest ribbon vertex to [16.4, 33, −50] is the candidate; if the medially-oriented placement is intended (prestriate cortex on the medial occipital surface around V1), the anchor should be pulled toward the medial surface rather than left 5.6 au deep in the occipital white matter. Verify residual < 1 au and re-check CLIP_BOUNDS before committing.
findings.notes: Not raised as 'wrong': the angular placement is anatomically sensible (Brodmann 18 surrounds 17 on and behind the occipital pole, and ctx-v1 at [9.5,17,−60] is 2.7 au from the surface), so this is a marker-depth defect rather than a wrong-gyrus claim.

findings.claimed: [33, 34, 2] — anchors.mesh 'ctx-hemisphere-l'
findings.expected: a point on the ribbon; the measured signed distance is +2.41 au, i.e. 2.41 au (2.9 mm) OUTSIDE the ctx-hemisphere-l surface, with the nearest vertex 2.41 au away
findings.basis: Measured against the committed mesh (ctx-hemisphere-l; nearest-vertex projection + normal sign). The sibling record that claims the same patch, ctx-a2 at [35, 33.5, 2], measures 0.57 au and is on the surface — so the two anchors for one anatomical patch differ by 2.9 au in depth, and the one that is registered as the surface landmark is the one that floats.
findings.suggestedFix: Pull the anchor onto the surface, e.g. x ≈ 34 at the same y/z (re-probe to confirm residual < 0.5 au), or re-use the ctx-a2 probe. Coordinate change only; the record's content is correct.
findings.notes: 2.9 mm is below the atlas' own plate/marker tolerance, so this is a small defect; it is reported because the record is the registered LANDMARK (surf-*) for the planum temporale and therefore the one that should be exact.

findings.claimed: [20.5, 23, 14] — contextNote: 'the ventral-most part of the pallidal cast at the level of the anterior commissure (x ≈ 20.5, y ≈ 23, z ≈ 14, an anchor placed on the baked globus-pallidus cast …)'
findings.expected: a point in the substantia innominata ventral to the anterior commissure; measured against the committed casts, [20.5, 23, 14] is OUTSIDE ctx-globus-pallidus-l (parity 0/6 along all six directions) and OUTSIDE ctx-putamen-l (0/6), and 2.1 au lateral of the globus pallidus' own x-maximum at that z (21.3…24.3 at z = 8, 21.3…23.8 at z = 0)
findings.basis: Measured against the committed meshes (ctx-globus-pallidus-l, ctx-putamen-l; ray-parity inside test and coronal bounding boxes, own measurement). The claim 'on the baked globus-pallidus cast' is therefore not true of the declared coordinate, and the coordinate also lands 3.91 au outside the hemisphere ribbon (irrelevant for a deep record, but it means no mesh owns the marker).
findings.suggestedFix: Either move the anchor to x ≈ 20, y ≈ 23, z ≈ 16 so it sits in the pallidal cast's ventral-anterior extension, or rewrite the parenthetical to what is true ('in the substantia innominata immediately ventral to the anterior commissure, lateral to the pallidal cast'). The anatomy the record describes (ventral pallidum in the substantia innominata, continuous with the subcommissural pallidum, principal output of the ventral striatopallidal system) is correct and should not be changed.
findings.notes: The name and the afferent/efferent set (accumbens → VP → MD thalamus; VP → lateral hypothalamus/VTA) are correct; the synonym list is the only other weak point ('ventral pallidum (substantia innominata component)' is right, but 'substantia innominata' is the region, not a synonym of the nucleus — leave as is unless the integrator wants the stricter wording).

findings.claimed: [22, 21, −2] with size3d [2.2, 3.5, 9] — function: 'the white-matter fringe on the medial-dorsal surface of the hippocampus'
findings.expected: a marker adjacent to the hippocampal dorsal surface; the nearest ctx-hippocampus-l vertex to this point is [22.98, 15.09, −3.96], 6.31 au away, and the hippocampal dorsal surface at z = −2 tops out at y = 14.2, so with size3d y-radius 3.5 the record's lower face (y = 17.5) sits 3.3 au clear of the structure it is declared to fringe
findings.basis: Measured against the committed mesh (ctx-hippocampus-l coronal bounding boxes and nearest-vertex projection, own measurement): at z = −2 (±1.5) the cast spans x 20.6…30.9, y 8.8…16.7. The fornix mesh (ctx-fornix-l) does rise to y 45 at this z, so the 'crus of the fornix' region is real, but the FIMBRIA's defining relation is contact with the hippocampus, and 6.3 au (7.6 mm) of separation defeats the marker.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to the hippocampal surface along its long axis, e.g. [25.0, 16.5, −4.0] (dorsal-medial surface of the body at residual < 1 au; the fimbria is the surface itself rather than a separate volume), keeping size3d. Re-probe against ctx-hippocampus-l before committing.
findings.notes: Everything textual in this record is correct (alveus from subiculum/CA1/CA3 → fimbria → crus → fornix → mammillary bodies and septum; anterior choroidal + PCA hippocampal supply; the choroidal-fissure surgical landmark).

findings.recordId: ctx-m1-toe, ctx-m1-leg, ctx-m1-trunk, ctx-m1-arm, ctx-m1-hand, ctx-m1-face, ctx-m1-tongue, ctx-m1-larynx, ctx-s1-toe … ctx-s1-larynx
findings.claimed: all 16 somatotopy records carry the identical level set ['lvl-tel-thalamostriate','lvl-tel-basal-ganglia','lvl-tel-centrum-semiovale','lvl-tel-convexity'] (y = 48, 58, 68, 78)
findings.expected: a per-segment level set, since the strips run from y = 58.2 (larynx) to y = 109.9 (toe): the toe segments occupy only lvl-tel-centrum-semiovale and lvl-tel-convexity, and no segment's own extent reaches y = 48
findings.basis: Internal contradiction — levels and origin3d/size3d are fields of the same record. ctx-m1-toe spans y 107…113 and ctx-s1-toe y 106…112, yet both offer a 'Levels (click to open plate + cut plane)' chip at y = 48 (InfoPanel.tsx LevelChips → gotoLevel), i.e. 59 au = 71 mm from the structure. The finest measured segment is ctx-m1-larynx at y 55…61 on the M1 side and ctx-s1-larynx at y 58…64 on the S1 side, so lvl-tel-basal-ganglia is defensible only for those two.
findings.suggestedFix: Derive each record's level set from its own extent: toe/leg/trunk/arm → lvl-tel-centrum-semiovale + lvl-tel-convexity; hand/face → those plus lvl-tel-convexity as already; tongue/larynx → add lvl-tel-basal-ganglia and keep lvl-tel-centrum-semiovale. One uniform set for sixteen segments is a copy-paste artifact, not a measured property.
findings.notes: The patch geometry itself needs no change: the ordering (somatotopicOrder 0…7 / rampT 1…0) is correct and the mediolateral march (x 7.33 → 50.86 on S1, 7.46 → 48.42 on M1) is monotone, which is exactly what the somatotopy overlay draws.

findings.claimed: absent — neither record has a connections object (both carry direction / modality / origin / target / decussation instead)
findings.expected: an explicit afferent/efferent pair, as the 23 records of tracts.json carry: 'afferent: retinal ganglion cells …; efferent: optic chiasm, optic tract, LGN, superior colliculus, pretectum, suprachiasmatic nucleus'
findings.basis: Field census (own measurement): 69 of the 71 telencephalon records carry connections; these two are the only two without, and both are 'tract'-kind records whose endpoints are already declared by origin/target/decussation. Whether the missing object is a defect depends on the loader contract for a structure-shaped tract record, which this audit did not establish.
findings.suggestedFix: Open question for the integrator, not a correction: if the InfoPanel renders a connections section for records that have one, add the object; if origin/target/decussation is the intended contract for a tract-shaped structure record, record that in docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md instead.
findings.notes: The content of origin/target/decussation in both records is correct (nasal 52–55 % crossing; the tract carrying the contralateral half-field; the tract itself not crossing).

findings.claimed: 'the macula — about 5 degrees of central vision — occupies roughly two-thirds of the axons' (nrv-cn2-optic) and the sibling phrasing in tract-optic-nerve ('the macula occupying about two-thirds of the fibres')
findings.expected: a sourced figure; the published range for the macular contribution to the optic-nerve fibre population is wide and the 'two-thirds' value is not a textbook constant
findings.basis: External, via web search: a meta-analysis of human optic-nerve fibre counts gives a mean of about 1.023 million axons with an inter-individual range of roughly 50 % of the mean (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11306597/), and the published count range quoted is 693,000–1,685,000 (https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/medicine-and-dentistry/optic-nerve-fiber); one review states foveal/macular fibres may be about 90 % of axons in the papillomacular bundle (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/62850). None of these settles a 'two-thirds of the axons for 5 degrees' figure, and the two records quote it as fact.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not change the number on this basis. Either attribute it in the record ('… about two-thirds of the axons (Publow/… )') or soften it to 'a large, disproportionate share of the axons'. Flagged for the integrator as an open quote, not a correction.
findings.notes: The related numeric claim 'roughly one million retinal ganglion cells from each eye' in tract-optic-nerve IS supported by the same meta-analysis (1.023 million mean) and needs no change.

findings.claimed: [0, 23.5, 23.5] — contextNote: 'anchored at the midline just above the sella … immediately anterior to the surf-optic-chiasm landmark record'
findings.expected: a placement consistent with the committed chiasm geometry; the committed ctx-optic-chiasm-l/-r pair measures y 10.4…18.6, z 14.3…23.5, so the mesh's own centre is ≈ [0, 14.5, 18.9]
findings.basis: Measured against the committed meshes (anatomy-manifest bboxes for ctx-optic-chiasm-l and ctx-optic-chiasm-r plus the GLB accessor min/max, own measurement): the anchor is 6.7 au (8.0 mm) above and 3.5 au (4.2 mm) behind the meshes it names, while the intra-orbital sibling record nrv-cn2-optic sits 0.46 au from the hemisphere ribbon and the tract-optic-nerve waypoints end at the anchor [2, 23.5, 23.5] — i.e. the record's own course line terminates at a point 6.7 au above the committed chiasm. Pre-existing divergence also recorded in PLAN.md §2.7.
findings.suggestedFix: Either re-anchor ctx-optic-chiasm and the last tract-optic-nerve waypoint to the committed chiasm centre (≈ [0, 16, 19], keeping the midline laterality and re-checking CLIP_BOUNDS), or state in the contextNote that the context record marks the surgical/chiasmatic-crossing site above the sella rather than the mesh centre. The record's clinical content (bitemporal hemianopia, junctional scotoma, chiasmal apoplexy, the 53 % crossing figure) is correct and was verified line by line.
findings.notes: The size3d [3.5, 1.2, 1.5] (7.0 × 2.4 × 3.0 au = 8.4 × 2.9 × 3.6 mm) is a plausible flattened-plate marker for this midline record; the committed mesh pair is far larger (12.3 au wide in total) because it is a baked surface pair, not a marker, so no size3d finding is made.

summary.countingNote: The two verdict and severity tables count the 20 entries of `findings` exactly as written: wrong 7 + suspect 11 + unverifiable-here 2 = 20, and major 5 + minor 15 = 20. No finding carries verdict 'ok' — the claims this audit checked and found sound are recorded in the separate `verifiedClaims` list (11 entries, each naming one or more records) rather than as 'ok' findings, so the verdict tables stay a list of defects and open questions, not of passes. Some findings name a list of recordIds (T3-0004 covers 8 records, T3-0017 covers 16), so per-record coverage is 71/71: every one of the 71 telencephalon records was read field by field.
